messages.subject: Re: Warning related with psi matrix
messages.body_plain:
Garret,

You might run the model with prisamp = TRUE, which draws samples from the priors. This could show you what the priors look like after taking into account positive definite constraints. The only affected priors would be the ones on the correlations within the psi matrix (which lead to covariances); instead of uniform from -1 to 1, they sometimes have more density around 0 to respect positive definite.

There is a recent bug that I fixed here; if it crashes for prisamp = TRUE, then also add meanstructure = TRUE to get it to run.

For the LCSM, there is a decent chance that this is a false alarm. I could say more if you send the output of

lavInspect(fit, 'est')$psi

where fit is your fitted model.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Exception: invese_spd: matrix not positive definite
messages.subject_clean: Exception: invese_spd: matrix not positive definite
messages.body_plain:
Julian,

Thanks for the report. I can reproduce this message, and it is related to the posterior predictive p-value computations. I think it happens because you have 24 observations in the data, and 24 variables are included in the model. So there is a 24x24 covariance matrix that is being computed from 24 simulated observations, which leads to the positive definite problems. I would be mildly surprised if this previously ran without issue, but to avoid the message you could add

test = "none"

to your blavaan() command.

It also looks like the default priors will not work well for your dataset, and perhaps the easiest thing to do is divide the entire dataset by 10. But, with only 24 observations, you probably want to give the priors good consideration because they will likely influence the posteriors.

Hope it helps,
Ed

Including a dummy code for each group is possible in OLS regression, but not in analyses of covariance structure (SEM).  The dummy codes are multicollinear: 1 of them equals 1 minus the sum of the others.  However, a multigroup model would be conceptually equivalent to having a dummy code for each group.  The effect of the grouping variable is reflected by differences in intercepts across groups.

https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.00747

There are multiple indirect effects of a polytomous grouping variable, just like there are multiple direct effects (any pairwise comparison among the 3 groups).
You can find some lavaan example syntax in a power-analysis tutorial I coauthored:

https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-022-01996-0

messages.body_plain:
The R2 values reported by summary() are not necessarily inappropriate, though they rely on the posterior mean and SD as opposed to the full posterior distribution. If you wanted to do something with the full posterior distribution of R2, you could use the ppmc() function. The code below assumes that "fit" is your fitted model:

rsqfun <- function(object) lavInspect(object, 'rsquare')

out <- ppmc(fit, discFUN = rsqfun)
summary(out)

## posterior samples of R2 in a matrix:
rsqsamps <- do.call("rbind", out@obsDist[[1]])

Ed

messages.subject: Proportion mediated in mediation analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I'm trying to do a mediation analysis and would like to compute the proportion mediated as follows:

# indirect effects
indirect_C1   := td*ct
# total effects
total_C1   := cd + td*ct
# proportion mediated
prop.mediated_C1   := indirect_C1 / total_C1

However, I receive the following error:
Error : The following error occured when compiling and adapting the model using rjags: Error in rjags::jags.model(model, data = dataenv, inits = inits, n.chains = length(runjags.object$end.state), : Error in node def[9,1,1] Invalid parent values

This is the relevant part of the model:
108 | def[1,1,1] <- beta[1,6,1] * beta[2,1,1] ... 112 | def[5,1,1] <- beta[2,6,1] + beta[1,6,1] * beta[2,1,1] ... 116 | def[9,1,1] <- def[1,1,1]/def[5,1,1]

Alas, I'm not very familiar with JAGS. But I suspect it has to do with the possibility of division by zero. If this is correct, one approach would be to use ifelse in JAGS (see e.g. here <https://sourceforge.net/p/mcmc-jags/discussion/610037/thread/800993b3/>). Is there a way to achieve this within blavaan? I thought about overriding the JAGS syntax with mcmcextra somehow, but I couldn't figure it out.

Any help is greatly appreciated!

All the best,
Paul
